findings.summary: The frontier chip labels in ai-stack.svg are painted #cf5f36 on the pale #faefeb chip fill, which measures 3.46:1, and 3.9:1 even on white. At the chip text's size that is under the 4.5:1 body-text floor, so a reader with reduced contrast sensitivity loses the tool name first; the purple deterministic chip beside them measures 5.5:1 and reads easily. A darker frontier ink, or near-black text inside the orange outline, would settle it.

agreement.svg sets the x axis to 0-140% while every bar is normalised to 100%, so 292 px of the 1400 px canvas is empty plot and the ticks at 120 and 140 mark values no row can take. The absolute row counts ('26 rows', '3 cross-structure') are placed inside that span, so a count sits on the percentage axis's own positional grammar and can read as a plotted value. A limit of 100 with the counts drawn outside the axes removes both readings.

pickup-probe.svg now wraps between words, which had repaired the earlier mid-word splits, but the wrapped remainder restarts at the block's left margin: 'source_id' and 'target_path' both continue at the same column as the opening brace, outdented past every key. A reader scanning the panel cannot tell at a glance that the line continues the one above rather than starting a new record. Indenting the continuation under its key's value column would keep the structure visible.

method: Each of the twelve attached PNG renders and the three attached GIFs was opened and read as a picture; no SVG and no other image was opened. Readings were then confirmed or corrected by measuring the named PNGs in memory: ink extents against all four canvas edges for every render, WCAG contrast of sampled colours, and an all-150-frame edge-contact scan of each GIF. Two candidate defects were withdrawn because the measurement did not support them: the IDS labels in mapping-flow.svg are masked by a 0.85-opacity white backing, and the pickup-probe continuation lines sit at the block margin rather than at x=0. Limitation: the three animations were judged from the frame the reader displays plus the frame-level edge scan, not from a viewing of all 150 frames, so motion-over-label overlap is reported only for the frames read.
